content:
A dummy ticket costs AED 49, AED 69 or AED 79 per traveller, and which one you pay depends only on how long you need the reservation to stay live. AED 49 buys two days of validity, AED 69 buys seven days and AED 79 buys 14 days. One way and return cost the same. There is no surcharge for a long-haul route, no surcharge for a second passenger beyond the per traveller price, and no booking fee bolted on at the end.

How much does a dummy ticket cost in the UAE?

Here are the three tiers and the situation each one is built for. Pick by the date your document will actually be read, not by the date you pay.

Price (per traveller)ValidityWho it suits
AED 492 daysAn appointment in the next day or two, a check-in desk tomorrow morning, or a border officer asking for proof of onward travel on a trip you are already taking
AED 697 daysThe common case: an appointment later this week or next, or a file that sits in a queue for a few days before anyone opens it
AED 7914 daysA submission at a busy visa centre, a file going to a consulate that batches applications, or an appointment you suspect may move

That is the whole price list for the reservation. If you also need the insurance line on a Schengen checklist, a genuine AXA policy starts at AED 30, and it is a separate product because it is a real policy that pays out rather than a document.

What exactly are you paying for?

A hard-facts summary before the detail.

ItemDetail
What it isA genuine airline reservation holding a seat under a live PNR, with the fare left unpaid
PriceAED 49 for 2 days, AED 69 for 7 days, AED 79 for 14 days, per traveller
One way vs returnSame price. The tier buys validity, not distance
Delivery10 to 15 minutes after payment, 24 hours a day
VerificationThe booking reference can be looked up in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport
Insurance (optional)AXA-issued cover from AED 30, meeting the EUR 30,000 medical minimum for Schengen
Accepted as evidenceThe Hellenic Embassy checklist for UAE applicants asks for a copy of flight ticket or flight reservation, including return flight

That last row is the part worth reading twice. Consulates ask for evidence of your travel arrangements, not for a purchased fare. The EU Visa Code sets out the supporting documents an applicant must produce, covering the purpose of the journey, accommodation, means of subsistence and enough information to judge whether you intend to leave again, in Article 14 of Regulation (EC) No 810/2009. The European Commission's own overview of applying for a Schengen visa describes supporting documents in those same terms.

Why is the price based on validity rather than the route?

Because nothing about the route costs us anything. No fare is paid, so a Dubai to Manila hold and a Dubai to Madrid hold are the same piece of work.

What does cost something is keeping the record alive. An unticketed reservation sits in an airline system with a ticketing deadline attached, and when that deadline passes the record is released automatically. The airline industry's reservations and ticketing procedures, published by IATA in the Passenger Services Conference Resolution Manual, include the enforced ticket time limit rules that make this happen.

So a longer validity is not a bigger document. It is a reservation that has to be held open, extended and monitored for longer, which is the only variable in the whole product. That is why you are quoted AED 49, AED 69 or AED 79 and nothing in between.

It is also why a return costs the same as a one way. Two flight segments under one reference is still one record with one deadline on it.

How do you pick the right tier for your appointment date?

Count the days between paying and the moment a human reads your file, then add a buffer. Most people get this wrong in the same direction, by buying for the day they submit instead of the day the file is reviewed.

Before you choose, have these in front of you:

  • The exact date and time of your appointment, or your flight if this is for check-in
  • Whether the centre reviews the file on the spot or forwards it to a consulate
  • Your passport, so the name on the reservation matches it exactly
  • The number of travellers, since the price is per traveller
  • The visa centre's own document checklist, because the wording varies by consulate
  • Any note from the centre about expected processing time in the current season

A rough rule. Appointment tomorrow or the day after, and the file is checked at the counter: AED 49 does the job. Appointment inside a week, or a file that goes into a queue: AED 69. Peak season, a centre with a backlog, or an appointment that might be rescheduled: AED 79 and stop worrying about it.

If you are unsure, the seven-day tier is the sensible default. The AED 20 difference between the two-day and seven-day tiers is a small price for not having a reservation lapse on the morning of your interview. You can book a reservation from AED 49 and have it in your inbox before you finish reading your checklist.

What does a free dummy ticket generator actually give you?

A PDF. That is the honest answer, and it is not a cheaper version of the same thing, it is a different thing.

The search for a free dummy ticket is completely reasonable. If you are paying a visa fee, insurance, maybe a translation and an attestation, trimming one line off the bill is a sane instinct. The problem is what the free tools are actually producing.

A generator builds an image of an itinerary. It fills a template with your name, a flight number and a date, and it looks right. What it cannot do is create a record inside an airline reservation system, because that requires access to the system and an actual booking. IATA's description of passenger name record data notes that a PNR can hold as little as a name, an itinerary and a ticket indicator. A generated PDF has none of that behind it. There is no record to find.

Which matters only at the moment someone checks. And someone does check, more often than people expect:

  • Visa centres and consulates look up booking references against the airline or the GDS, especially where an applicant has been refused before
  • Check-in agents enter the reference to confirm you have onward travel before they board you
  • Border officers in countries that require proof of onward travel ask for the reference and verify it

A fabricated document that returns nothing is worse than no document at all, because now there is a question mark over your file rather than a gap in it. This is the real distinction, and it has nothing to do with price. A reservation is a genuine booking with the fare unpaid. A generated PDF is a picture of a booking that was never made. The first is a normal part of a visa application. The second is a misrepresentation, and it can follow you through later applications.

You can test any reservation yourself before you submit it. Enter the booking reference and surname in the traveller lookup for Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport and see whether a live record comes back. A flight itinerary with a verifiable PNR will return your name, route and dates. Do this once and the difference between the two products becomes obvious.

Is it cheaper to buy a refundable fare instead?

Almost never, and the comparison is not really about the cash.

A fully flexible fare out of Dubai is typically several hundred to a few thousand dirhams, and that money leaves your account the day you book. You get it back later, if the fare class really is refundable, if you cancel inside the window, and if you accept the cancellation charge. Semi-flexible fares look cheaper and then keep a slice of your money.

Then there is the timing problem. The US Department of State tells visitor visa applicants plainly that issuance is never certain and that they should not make final travel plans or buy tickets until the visa is in hand, on its visitor visa page. The sequence most people want, buy a ticket to prove the trip and then get the visa, is the opposite of what the consulate advises.

A refundable fare is the right choice in exactly one situation: where the airline or the border demands a paid onward ticket rather than a reservation. Some carriers do, on some routes, and when they do, a held reservation will not satisfy them. Check the airline's own condition of carriage for the route before you fly, and if a paid ticket is required, buy one.

For everything else, a reservation answers the question the consulate actually asked. The full comparison is three numbers wide.

OptionWhat you payWhat it costs you if plans change
Our reservationAED 49, AED 69 or AED 79 per travellerNothing. It expires on its own, and we reissue free if your appointment moves
Refundable airline fareThe full fare up front, in the hundreds or thousands of dirhamsA cancellation charge, plus weeks waiting for the refund to land
Free generated PDFNothingA document that returns no record when checked, and a credibility problem on your file

What else is in the bill, and what is not ours?

The reservation is usually the smallest line on a visa budget. It helps to see the fees separately, because the ones you cannot avoid are not the ones you are shopping for.

CostWho charges itAmount
Flight reservationUsAED 49, AED 69 or AED 79 per traveller
Travel insuranceUs, policy issued by AXAFrom AED 30
Hotel reservation for a visa fileUs, arranged by email at info@thedummyticket.aeQuoted on request
Schengen visa feeThe consulateEUR 90 for adults, EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 12, per the European Commission
Visa centre service feeThe outsourced centre, such as VFS Global or BLS InternationalSet by the centre, varies by consulate
Translations and attestationsThird partiesVaries by document

We sell documents. We do not prepare, file or track applications, so nothing on the consulate side of that table passes through us.

Why do applications still get refused when the reservation is fine?

Because the reservation was never the thing being judged. No document decides a visa, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling you something.

Refusals turn on the things a consular officer weighs: whether your funds plausibly cover the trip, whether your ties to the UAE make it likely you will come back, and whether the story your file tells is consistent. The avoidable mistakes we see are mundane.

  • The reservation expired before the file was reviewed, usually a two-day tier bought for a queue that took a week
  • The name on the reservation does not match the passport, often a middle name added or dropped
  • The dates on the reservation contradict the hotel booking or the leave letter
  • Bank statements show a lump sum deposited days before the application
  • The insurance policy falls short of the EUR 30,000 medical minimum, or leaves repatriation out
  • Nationality changes the requirement and the applicant worked from a checklist written for someone else

That last one catches people. A UAE resident on an Indian or Pakistani passport faces different documentation from an Emirati national for the same destination, and the centre's checklist for your nationality is the one that counts. If a question about validity or verification is nagging at you, the FAQ covers it in more detail.

What if your appointment moves, or the consulate cannot verify it?

Two different situations, two different answers, and both are worth knowing before you pay.

Your appointment is rescheduled. We reissue the reservation with the new dates free of charge. Email info@thedummyticket.ae with the booking reference and the new date and you get a fresh document. There is no charge and no second purchase, so a moved appointment is not a reason to buy the expensive tier defensively.

The reservation failed you. There is one case where we refund in full: where a refusal letter states that the reservation had expired or could not be verified. That is our mistake and we own it.

What is not covered, stated plainly so there are no surprises. A change of plans is not refundable. A refusal on any other ground is not refundable, and that includes refusals on funds, on ties, on travel history, on an incomplete file or on a decision the officer did not explain. The refund exists for a reservation that did not do its job, not for an application that did not succeed.

Verification deserves one honest note too. The booking reference can be checked in Amadeus, Sabre or Travelport, and that is the reliable lookup. Some airlines show an unpaid hold under Manage Booking and many never do, so a blank result on an airline website does not mean the record is missing. If you need proof of onward travel at a check-in desk or a border, an onward ticket is the same reservation sold for that moment.

faqs.question: How much does a dummy ticket cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: AED 49 for two days of validity, AED 69 for seven days and AED 79 for 14 days, per traveller. One way and return cost the same. Nothing is added at checkout, and travel insurance is a separate product starting at AED 30.

faqs.question: Why does a return cost the same as a one way?
faqs.answer: Because no fare is being paid, so the route adds no cost. Two segments under one booking reference is still one record with one ticketing deadline on it. You are paying for how long that record is held open, not for distance.

faqs.question: Is a free dummy ticket generator worth trying?
faqs.answer: It gives you a PDF with no reservation behind it, so there is no record for anyone to look up. That is a different product, not a cheaper one. Consulates, check-in agents and border officers do verify booking references, and a document that returns nothing hurts your file.

faqs.question: Which validity should I buy for a visa appointment?
faqs.answer: Buy for the day your file is read, not the day you submit. Two days at AED 49 suits an appointment tomorrow checked at the counter. Seven days at AED 69 is the safe default. Fourteen days at AED 79 suits a backlog or a movable date.

faqs.question: Can I get a refund if my visa is refused?
faqs.answer: Only in one case: where the refusal letter says the reservation had expired or could not be verified. Refusals on funds, ties, travel history or an incomplete file are not refundable, and neither is a change of plans. Rescheduled appointments get a free reissue.
